data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'f-r-h', meaning 'to be raised above'. This name signifies victory and triumph over adversity. The name Farih carries the meaning “Victorious” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Farih usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Farih belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victorious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Farih total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference:
Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah records the name Farih ibn Malik Al-Ashja'i, a renowned poet in pre-Islamic Arabia. His poetry was one of the last prominent expressions of pre-Islamic Arabian culture, which was largely displaced by the rise of Islam in the Arabian Peninsula.
Time period: Pre-Islamic Arabia (5th–7th centuries CE)
Context: Poet and cultural figure

Ibn Qayyim Al-Jawziyya, a prominent Islamic scholar, mentions Farih ibn Al-Harith Al-Ataki, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. He was one of the early converts to Islam in Yemen and is known for his devotion and piety. He was also a teacher and scholar who played an important role in spreading the teachings of Islam in Yemen.
Time period: Early Islamic period (7th century CE)
Context: Companion of the Prophet Muhammad, scholar and teacher
